summary.text: 马 is the standardized simplified form corresponding to 馬, whose graph depicts a horse as a whole animal. Its current common meaning is “horse.”

formation.text: 馬 is pictographic: the graph depicts the horse as a whole, with visible features described as its eye, mane, body, tail, and legs. No separate semantic or phonetic components are supported. This is the construction of 馬, the traditional graph corresponding to 马.

history.text: The curated Shang-style oracle-bone and mid-Western Zhou bronze-style redrawings illustrate different historical forms of 馬, retaining recognizable horse features. They are illustrations of forms, not evidence of a direct line of descent; the inspected account does not date the earliest individual inscription.
馬 corresponds to simplified 马. One account says the simplified form follows a cursive form, but the inspected character-specific evidence does not establish that precise pathway or its chronology.

uncertainties.text: The evidence supports a whole-animal pictograph, but does not establish the earliest dated inscription or earliest attested lexical use. The Shuowen description of head, mane, tail, and four legs is a historical interpretation, not independent proof of the earliest graphic details.
Although “big” and surname are listed among later senses, the dossier supplies no verified dates or evidence establishing their development from “horse.”

senses.text: The character's recorded common meaning is “horse”; the available evidence does not date its earliest lexical use.
Surname is a recorded use, but its earliest attestation and relation to the word for “horse” are not established here.

limitations.text: The dossier does not establish dated attestations for later senses or a supported semantic path from “horse” to surname or other proposed extensions.

overview.text: 馬 depicts a horse as a whole animal; 马 is its standardized simplified form. The common meaning is “horse.”

relationships.text: 馬 is the traditional graph corresponding to standardized simplified 马. The cited material does not establish the exact cursive pathway or its chronology.
